conventions.convention: A finite microstate model has a finite nonempty state set and a finite numerical energy map ε; physical energy is ε J. Distinct states with equal energies remain distinct microstates. Internal-energy interpretation requires separately supplied compatible center-of-mass mechanical data.

Temperature is positive, β = 1/(k_B T), k_B retains its exact SI value, partition functions are dimensionless, and canonical sampling is an adopted preparation rule with no dynamical equilibration conclusion.

Regular-shell preparation uses dimensionless canonical coordinates, a C2 numerical Hamiltonian, compact inverse images of compact energy intervals, nonzero energy gradient, AC, and a nonempty shell with positive finite coarea mass. Preparation itself imposes no global-flow hypothesis.
The finite microcanonical window uses |E(x) − E0| ≤ δ with δ ≥ 0; it must be nonempty, including when δ = 0. The regular-shell branch instead adopts normalized coarea measure and assumes AC.

Measurable canonical entropy is relative to the declared dimensionless reference measure; it is not automatically a macroscopic entropy. The underlying measure-space definition does not assume completeness.
Lattice pressure means the assigned quantity (k_B T/v0)L^(−d) log Z_L for bounded finite-range translation-invariant finite-alphabet cubic models, not an identified mechanical pressure.

The general quantum identities use the G = H branch, AC and Countable Choice, a semibounded self-adjoint Hamiltonian, positive finite Gibbs trace, and a local summable moment envelope. Mean, variance and entropy are spectral sums, not unqualified traces of unbounded products.

Finite mode collections have m ≥ 1, positive excitation energies, bosonic occupations starting at zero or fermionic occupations in {0,1}, and an explicitly defined additive diagonal Hamiltonian on its squared-weight domain.
Dephasing is convergence of Cesaro state averages in trace norm; projections retain whole degenerate energy eigenspaces. Neither pointwise relaxation nor a Gibbs limit is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite microstate model at T > 0, adopt Pβ(x) = exp(−βE(x))/Z(β), β = 1/(k_B T). Countable or measurable versions are assigned only when their declared partition sum or integral is positive and finite.
For the adopted canonical law on a fixed finite nonempty state set and fixed energy list, −∂β log Z = Ēβ, ∂β² log Z = Varβ(E), Sβ = k_B(log Z + βĒβ), and Fstat = −k_B T log Z = Ēβ − TSβ.

Under AC, Countable Choice and the adopted quantum Gibbs preparation, the explicitly defined finite independent positive-energy mode collection has positive finite trace Z = ∏r Zr, factorized occupation-basis law, and the corresponding one-mode means q/(1−q) for bosons and q/(1+q) for fermions.

In the G = H Gibbs branch, assuming AC, Countable Choice, semibounded self-adjoint H, positive finite Gibbs trace and the stated local moment envelope, the spectral mean, variance and entropy are finite and satisfy the canonical log-partition identities and Fstat = Ēβ − TSvN.

Under AC, a C2 numerical Hamiltonian on the specified dimensionless canonical chart with a regular compact-shell band defines the normalized coarea shell law νÊ when the shell is nonempty and its coarea mass is positive and finite.

For the specified bounded finite-range lattice model at fixed positive temperature and fixed cell volume, pL = L^(−d) log ZL and PL = (k_B T/v0)pL have finite limits; a pointwise boundary-energy perturbation bounded by Cb L^(d−1) has the same limit.

For two finite models at the same T > 0 whose declared composite state set is the Cartesian product and whose energy is additive without interaction, ZAB = ZAZB, PAB = PAPB, SAB = SA + SB, and FAB = FA + FB.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 invokes a 'positive-basis trace convention in [F1]' to identify the full trace with the occupation-weight sum and conclude trace finiteness. The cited Gibbs postulate assumes trace-class existence; it does not state the converse diagonal-summability criterion. The finite-box argument correctly proves summability, but the intervening deduction that the bounded positive diagonal operator is trace class is implicit. A finite-rank/nuclear-series argument closes this short gap.

The Statement declares φt to be the physical flow from the shell definition, whose domain is in Ophys, but applies it directly to Borel A ⊆ ΣÊ, a shell in the dimensionless domain O. The intended coordinate identification is clear, but the displayed invariance equation needs the conjugated dimensionless flow at t/(1 s), or a physical-shell pushforward of νÊ.

The Statement assigns Ei units of joules but writes the envelope as (1 + |Ei|²)exp(−βEi). The addition of dimensionless 1 and an energy squared needs an explicit numerical-energy convention, such as Êi = Ei/(1 J), with the corresponding numerical inverse-temperature parameter. The intended summability condition and conclusions are otherwise sound.

The Statement types E as joule-valued and then uses (1 + |E|²)exp(−βE) in the domination hypothesis. Explicitly use the numerical energy E/(1 J), or a dimensionally homogeneous replacement, when matching the real-valued mathematical supplier.

The local moment-envelope hypothesis adds 1 to |Ej|² while Ej are declared physical energy eigenvalues in joules. The numerical-coordinate conversion used explicitly in the finite-mode theorem should also be stated here when applying the real-valued trace-Gibbs supplier.

alerts.finding: Proof 1.2 calls (u,v) ↦ ⟨u,u0⟩⟨v,v0⟩ 'C-linear on H × K'. This map is bilinear, not linear on the product vector space: for nonzero u0,v0, its values at (u0,0) and (0,v0) are zero while its value at their sum is positive. The subsequent tensor-quotient argument uses bilinearity, so this is a wording defect rather than a failure of the tensor construction.

seams_checked.note: The continuum page proves a free-cube grand-pressure limit for stable power-tempered pair interactions. The bridge remark explicitly distinguishes this contextual prerequisite from its bounded finite-range lattice theorem and infers no continuum limit from the lattice result.

Shell preparation retains AC, compact regular bands, nonempty shells and normalized coarea measure. Invariance adds smoothness and full-band invertible flow. Dephasing retains the discrete finite-multiplicity trace-class interface and Cesaro-only conclusion. The physical/dimensionless flow notation concern is recorded separately.

The potentials page defines local macroscopic Legendre transforms on valid inverse-coordinate charts. The bridge consistently declines to identify statistical −k_B T log Z with those macroscopic potentials without an additional model bridge.

The microscopic-entropy definition faithfully repeats the finite nonempty state set and numerical-to-joule energy assignment and explicitly supplies neither sampling nor a macroscopic entropy identification.

The driven model preserves the finite-state and rest-frame qualifications. Protocol preparation and Jarzynski use only the finite canonical branch at positive bath temperature, with finite energies and positive finite partition sums; no relaxation claim is imported.

The ensemble postulate specializes the measurable canonical rule to the measurable finite-energy configuration subset with restricted reference measure and positive finite normalizer. It separately declares zero weight at infinite energy and separately adopts grand-canonical and positional-shell laws.
